svg.title: Who was to calculate the interest? Three Bohemia records, 1997–2007
svg.desc: An original evidence diagram with three dated cards. The former Bohemia law assigned the Legislative Auditor a role in calculating a rate based on levee-district investment returns. Louisiana Act 130 of June 22, 2005 struck that former wording. A February 28, 2007 federal court order reported the auditor declined to calculate interest under the 2000 settlement and identified Bourgeois Bennett as the state-court-approved disbursing agent whose calculations were offered by the claimants. These facts do not prove that the legislative change alone caused the disagreement or that claimants received final payments. The federal damages judgment was reversed July 23, 2007.

Primary sources: Louisiana Legislature, Act 130 of 2005 (SB210), enrolled pp.3–4 https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=317802 ; United States District Court, Eastern District of Louisiana, Case 2:06-cv-03829, Document 154 filed 2007-02-28, pp.3–4 https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-laed-2_06-cv-03829/pdf/USCOURTS-laed-2_06-cv-03829-1.pdf ; United States Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit, 07-30086 filed 2007-07-23, pp.9–11 https://cases.justia.com/federal/appellate-courts/ca5/07-30086/920070723/0.pdf . License: all rights reserved to Final Vestige Studios for original vector composition. Accessible alt: Three dated legal records show a former statutory interest-rate duty being removed and a later dispute over who could calculate settlement interest; no beneficiary payment is established. Suggested caption: The interest calculation changed legal footing between 2005 and 2007. Act 130 struck an earlier statutory audit provision; a later federal order reported contested accounting authority. Graphic: Final Vestige Studios, based on cited primary records; not a depiction of a historical document or proof of payment.
